title: Largest Rectangle In Histogram
description:
A histogram has one-unit-wide bars with nonnegative integer heights in heights. Return the greatest area of a rectangle contained entirely under adjacent bars. A rectangle may span one or more consecutive bars; its height cannot exceed the shortest bar in its span.

An empty histogram has area zero, as does a histogram whose bars are all height zero. Width is a count of bars, not a difference in height. The maximum need not use the tallest bar: several medium bars can form a larger rectangle than a single peak.

For each bar, imagine how far it could extend in both directions before meeting a shorter bar. A monotone stack of indices records candidate left boundaries; when a shorter bar arrives, taller candidates have just found their right boundary and their maximal areas can be calculated.

Example 1:

Input: heights = [2,1,5,6,2,3]
Output: 10

Example 2:

Input: heights = [2,4]
Output: 4

Example 3:

Input: heights = []
Output: 0

Constraints:

  • 0 <= heights.length <= 100,000.
  • 0 <= heights[i] <= 10,000.
  • Areas fit within a signed 32-bit integer for the supplied tests.
